Looping in technical notes that should be in the runbook:

- Runbook owner: Rishi (runtime health + rollback to previous model weight)
- Cutover steps (high level):
  1) Pre-cutover validation on staging (smoke tests, perf baseline)
  2) Scale dedicated pool to N+1 capacity by 02:00 PT on 03/17
  3) Deploy model_variant v1.3 (canary to 5% traffic for 30m)
  4) Ramp to 100% over 2 hours if no regression alerts
  5) Post-cutover verification (latency, error rate, token cost check)

- Rollback triggers: sustained 2x latency increase above baseline, error rate >2% for 15m, or major quality regression flagged by the evaluation harness. Rollback action: immediate traffic re-route to stable variant and trigger incident bridge.

I'll attach a short runbook draft (go-live-runbook-draft.md) with checklists for pre/post steps. I recommend we define a single incident commander for the entire cutover window (suggest Connor).

-rishi

Hi team —

Quick procurement update: I received the redlines from Acme (attached SOW-redlines.pdf). Two items to note that affect the go-live timing:

1) Data retention clause needs clarification; Acme wants 90-day cache retention while we default to 30. We'll propose a narrow exception for the project with audit logging enabled.
2) SLA credit language: procurement wants to avoid broad financial exposure for an initial pilot. We can set a service-level target and a remediation plan instead of credits for 90 days post-launch.

DocuSign prep is ready; I will share a live DocuSign link once we agree on these two bullets. If procurement needs extra reviews, that could push formal signature by up to 5 business days, which would impact a 03/17 go-live.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Head of Contracts | Redwood Inference
